title: Conference Reviewer Assignment under COI, Entity Resolution, and Capacity Constraints
summary: Assign 3 reviewers to each active conference submission (150 papers, 6 withdrawn; 60 reviewers, 6 unavailable) under tight capacity, four conflict-of-interest rules, seniority coverage, and canonical-institution diversity. Institution strings are aliases resolved via a gazetteer and coauthor names appear in three documented formats, so the conflict set must be derived, not string-matched. A second deliverable (conflict_audit.csv, exact triple F1) externalizes the derivation. Any hard violation scores 0; full marks require an optimal assignment plus a perfect audit.
taskPrompt:
You are assisting the program chairs of a peer-reviewed conference with reviewer assignment.

Input data lives in input/: submissions.csv (150 papers including withdrawn ones), reviewers.csv (60 reviewers including unavailable ones), coauthorships.csv, declared_conflicts.csv, and institutions.csv (the alias-to-canonical institution gazetteer). Read input/README.md (the data dictionary: institution strings are aliases, author names appear in several formats, and status/availability columns matter) and then input/constraints.md (the authoritative rules and the exact scoring formula).

Two deliverables:
1. output/assignment.csv - header `paper_id,reviewer_id`, exactly 3 reviewers for every ACTIVE paper, satisfying load limits, four kinds of conflict-of-interest rules, seniority coverage, and canonical-institution diversity. Any single hard-constraint violation scores 0.
2. output/conflict_audit.csv - header `reviewer_id,paper_id,reason_code`, every conflicted pair over available reviewers x active papers with all applicable reason codes; graded by exact triple F1.

`python3 software/check_format.py <assignment> [<audit>]` validates schemas only.

Reviewer capacity is tight and conflicts are dense; feasibility itself is a global problem, full marks require an optimal assignment plus a perfect audit, and every entity comparison is defined on canonical forms, so derive the conflict set carefully.
agentMustDo: Read input/README.md and input/constraints.md before touching the data; institution strings are aliases and all institution logic is canonical via institutions.csv.

Derive the full conflict set over available reviewers x active papers: canonical-affiliation matches, co-authorship in 2023 or later under the three documented name formats, declared conflicts, and reviewers who are themselves authors.
Respect the status and available columns: withdrawn papers and unavailable reviewers must not be assigned and are outside the audit domain.

Produce an assignment satisfying every hard constraint: exactly 3 distinct reviewers per active paper, loads within max_load, no conflicted pair, at least one senior reviewer per paper, and three distinct canonical institutions per paper.
Maximize total affinity as defined in constraints.md; near-optimal total affinity is required for a high score.
Write output/assignment.csv (paper_id,reviewer_id) and output/conflict_audit.csv (reviewer_id,paper_id,reason_code with every applicable code).

inputFiles.name: submissions.csv
inputFiles.description: 150 papers: paper_id, title, status (active/withdrawn), primary_area, |-separated topics, and authors as 'Name (Affiliation); ...' with alias affiliations.

inputFiles.name: reviewers.csv
inputFiles.description: 60 reviewers: reviewer_id, name, alias affiliation, |-separated areas and topics, seniority, max_load, available (yes/no).

inputFiles.name: coauthorships.csv
inputFiles.description: Reviewer-author co-authorship records with year; names in 'First Last', 'Last, First', or 'F. Last' form; only years >= 2023 create conflicts.

inputFiles.name: declared_conflicts.csv
inputFiles.description: Explicitly declared (reviewer_id, paper_id) conflicts, including inert distractor rows for withdrawn papers and unavailable reviewers.

inputFiles.name: README.md
inputFiles.description: Data dictionary: column semantics, alias rules, and the exact name-matching rules.

inputFiles.name: constraints.md
inputFiles.description: Authoritative rules: hard constraints, audit specification, affinity formula, and the published scoring formula.

referenceFiles.name: scoring.json
referenceFiles.description: Hidden optimal total affinity (computed by exact MILP via HiGHS) plus scoring weights.

referenceFiles.name: optimal_assignment.csv
referenceFiles.description: One optimal feasible assignment achieving the optimal affinity.

referenceFiles.name: conflict_audit.csv
referenceFiles.description: The true (reviewer_id, paper_id, reason_code) triple set over the audit domain.

evaluation: Deterministic. The grader independently rebuilds canonical entities and the conflict-code set, then checks every hard constraint on assignment.csv; any violation scores 0. Otherwise score = 0.25 + 0.45 * q + 0.30 * audit_f1, where q = clamp((A - 0.9*OPT) / (0.1*OPT), 0, 1), A is the submitted total affinity, OPT is the exact MILP optimum stored in reference/scoring.json, and audit_f1 is the exact F1 of submitted (reviewer_id, paper_id, reason_code) triples against the hidden truth set. Known-good replay: output_test_pos scores 1.0, output_test_neg (one conflicted pair, no audit) scores 0.0.
